summary: SDK auto-loads suspiciously-named third-party dependency at import with silenced errors
details: On import of the package's main entry, client.js unconditionally calls initializeProvider(), which dynamically imports the third-party npm package 'htps-provider' and instantiates HttpProvider(). Errors from the import and constructor are silently swallowed inside a try/catch, and a misleading 'Server is running successfully!' log is emitted regardless of outcome. The dependency name is a one-character near-miss of the common 'https-provider' term and is not referenced anywhere in the package's advertised ethers-based marketplace functionality or README. package.json also declares 'crypto' (a known placeholder/squat name on npm) as a runtime dependency alongside 'htps-provider'. Requiring or importing this SDK therefore causes attacker-selectable code from 'htps-provider' to execute in the installer's Node process at import time, with any errors hidden behind a cover-story log line.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
